newsitem.title: UK: Reporter ousts former UK minister hit by sleaze.
newsitem.headline: Reporter ousts former UK minister hit by sleaze.

text.p: Former BBC war reporter Martin Bell won the fifth safest seat held by the ruling Conservatives in the British election, beating a former minister, Neil Hamilton.

Bell, who stood as an independent and was supported by the Labour Party and Liberal Democrats, won by an astonishing 11,077 votes. Hamilton denied allegations that he took money from a businessman to ask questions in parliament.

Bell, who had said that standing for election was more frightening than dodging bullets in Sarajevo's "sniper alley," pledged that he would remain an independent and would stand for one term of office only.
"I believe you have lit a beacon that will illuminate some dark corners including in the mother of parliaments herself," he told the people of Tatton in his acceptance speech.
Hamilton, said he was "devastated" by the result."
Nationally, Labour was heading for a landslide victory to end 18 years of Conservative government.
